inputs.absolute_divergence_subsequence: m=6k, so Lambda(6k)=0; compare eventual Laguerre leading term against sum_k (log k)^(n-1)/k

bellotti.use_scope: sufficient boundary source for fixed n only

exact_definitions.von_mangoldt: Lambda(m)=log p if m=p^j for a prime p and integer j>=1; Lambda(m)=0 otherwise

inputs.finite_identity: For real 1<=X<Y that are not positive integers, sum_{X<m<=Y} a_m b_n(m) = A(Y)b_n(Y)-A(X)b_n(X) - integral_X^Y A(t)b_n'(t)dt.

proof_obligations.obligation: derive the displayed finite half-open identity with X,Y nonintegral and exact A(X),A(Y) terms
derive b_n'(t)=t^(-2)[(L_{n-1}^{(1)})'(log t)-L_{n-1}^{(1)}(log t)] and bound it by C_n(1+log t^(n-1))/t^2 for fixed n
from Bellotti v1 Theorem 1.5 and equations (1.3)-(1.4), derive for sufficiently large x |A(x)|<=1+C x exp(-d(log x)^(3/5)/(log log x)^(1/5))
combine O2-O3 with fixed n to prove A(Y)b_n(Y)->0
combine O2-O3 with fixed n to prove integral_X^infinity |A(t)b_n'(t)|dt<infinity
take Y to infinity only after O1,O4,O5 and preserve original integer order

for m=6k, prove Lambda(m)=0 because 6k has at least prime factors 2 and 3, so |a_m|=1; use the leading coefficient (-1)^(n-1)/(n-1)! of L_{n-1}^{(1)} to obtain |b_n(6k)|>=c_n(log k)^(n-1)/k for all sufficiently large k; conclude divergence of the absolute subseries, including n=1
